 YTU is taking giant steps in the field of sustainability for a better future. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 The Best and the Most Efficient Sustainability Practices 
 From this point of view, it continues to generate new ideas and encourage exciting innovations through interdisciplinary collaboration while developing solutions for global challenges. In its innovation and commercialization studies, YTU continues its efforts to produce innovative solutions in systems such as solar energy and hydrogen energy, which are renewable energy sources, and carries out pioneering activities in this field. In addition, it contributes to research and policy development on human effects on climate change, developing social projects, and making progress towards a more sustainable future. Besides, YTU continues to work on modeling an institutional path to a more sustainable campus. Yıldız Technical University Sustainability Plan is a critical and necessary step to building a more sustainable future. In this context, the University established the Sustainable Campus Commission and prepared the "Yıldız Technical University Sustainable Campus Report 2020" under the editorship of Commission President Prof. Dr. Çiğdem Polatoğlu. 
 Sustainability Activities in 2020 
 YTU established the "Sustainable Campus Commission" in order to carry out its sustainability activities in a systematic and planned manner. Yıldız Technical University has announced its environmental sustainability efforts in 2020 at www.kampus.yildiz.edu.tr, focusing on the “Sustainable Campus”. Accordingly, it shared its sustainable goals based on four main concepts: Smart, Green, Non-Handicapped and Sustainable. With its green campus approach, it has the characteristics of a sustainable campus with a solution to regional environmental problems, reduction of the effects of climate change, disaster management, self-sufficient energy system, waste management, protection of water, and creation of ecological awareness. Yıldız Technical University, which has been continuing its studies in line with the "Greenmetric Sustainability Indices" since 2016, has determined its study subjects as Campus and Infrastructure, Energy and Climate Change, Waste, Water, Transportation, Education, and Research.

 A greener Campus with efficient resource management 
 Correct Energy Production and Consumption 
 Depletion of limited resources, the need for energy resources and the owner of greenhouse gas emissions; these makes it more important day by day to control these resources accurately and efficiently. During these periods, Yıldız Technical University evaluates the current energy level each year and determines new strategies, targets and plans for the coming years. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 32 
 MWh 
 Average Daily Consumption of 
Davutpaşa Campus 
 
 3 
 M 
 TL 
 Research Budget for 
Sustainability 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 Energy Policies of YTU; 
 
 Preferring products with high energy efficiency 
 Replacing existing devices with high-efficiency devices 
 Use and dissemination of renewable resources 
 The implementation of green and smart systems in new buildings to be built. 
 
 One of the sine qua non of sustainability is how the existing resources are managed… Using resources efficiently and with the least harm to the environment, choosing renewable resources should be everyone's priority… With this understanding, YTU attaches importance to the use of clean energy in every area it comes into contact with, starting from its campuses. 
 LED lighting is used in all buildings of YTU, and all of the lightings are photocells, that is, they flash automatically. In this way, energy consumption is reduced. On the other hand, the devices preferred in laboratories, faculties, administrative buildings, sports halls, libraries and dining halls are devices with "Class A" certificate and low energy consumption. 
 Meters to monitor electricity consumption instantly, to prevent electricity leaks and to disable self-deactivation in case of electricity leakage, are the two basic elements of the electricity infrastructure at YTU. 
 Heating and cooling systems constitute a large part of energy needs. According to 2019 data, the daily average electrical energy consumption of Davutpaşa Campus is 32 MWh. The air conditioners on the campus are centrally managed depending on the summer and winter months. Despite the energy savings due to the use of central systems in heating and cooling, energy consumption is still high. For this reason, studies are planned for natural ventilation and renewal of insulations in buildings. 
 Unlike the historical buildings on the campus, natural lighting was given importance in the newly constructed buildings. These buildings contain a high amount of windows, including the roofs, to maximize daylight use. Thus, there is no need for lighting during the day and energy consumption is reduced. 
  
 Renewable Energy Strategies 
 Yıldız Technical University, aiming to provide an environment with low carbon density and high quality life for all its employees and students, and also aiming to reach by the year 2030 with “100% Clean Energy”, has been investing to increase the use of clean and renewable energy resources. 
With the 3 MW Solar Energy System Project prepared by YTU, 7 thousand 758 PV modules will be installed in car parks, bus stops and buildings. The feasibility studies of the project (Solar Energy System Project), have been completed, legal approvals and permissions have been taken and a Connection Agreement to the Distribution System for Unlicensed Electricity Producers has been signed with the electricity distribution company. 
 
The 11 buildings in the project were included in the scope of the “Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings Project” of the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization and were entitled to receive support. Accordingly, the costs of energy efficiency measures to be gained from these buildings and the investment cost of the solar energy system to be established will be covered within the Ministry grant. The total contribution of the project to YTU is expected to be 50 million TL in the first phase. 
 
Yıldız Technical University, designing its buildings on the basis of minimum energy consumption and applying efficiency-enhancing practices of national and international energy efficiency standards, has identified the energy efficiency measures to be taken by conducting energy audits in all its buildings. Buildings are classified as C class in energy performance and B class in greenhouse gas emission performance. In addition, energy identity certificates were issued for the buildings. 
 
An application was made to the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources to become an Energy Efficiency Services Authorized Institution in order to contribute to increasing energy efficiency in buildings. In this context, six faculty members received study-project certification training and were defined as educators, taking into account the course contents and subject matters defined by the Ministry.

 We Reduce Waste Generation 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The First University to Receive a "Zero Waste Certificate" in Istanbul 
 Rapid population growth, environmental pollution caused by increasing demands and lack of resources are among the most important problems of the age we are in... With this awareness, Yıldız Technical University takes many steps supported by R&D studies in order to bring waste to the circular economy. Zero Waste application was initiated by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in order to prevent waste in Turkey, to use natural resources more efficiently, to reduce the amount of waste formation and to improve the separation of wastes at source. Based on this practice and for a greener, cleaner campus, many strategies have been created, including effective management of Yıldız Technical University waste, reducing waste generation and separating it at source. Yıldız Technical University, which has been a part of the Zero Waste project since 2018, established the Zero Waste Management System at Davutpaşa Campus and became the first state university in Istanbul to be entitled to receive the "Zero Waste Certificate". 
 How Does YTU Manage Its Waste? 
 Accepting the waste management hierarchy as a guide, YTU has implemented many practices to prevent waste generation, especially the use of paper, with the aim of reducing waste. With all official correspondence carried out through the Electronic Document Management System (EBYS), the University saves both stationery costs and waste generation and ensures that correspondence is archived in a healthy way. 
 Effective and Fast System in the Management of Solid Wastes 
 Within the scope of the activities carried out by the student clubs, it is ensured that the reuse and recycling of waste is supported. In this context, used books are sent to those in need, plastic covers are collected to support the production of electric chairs for disabled individuals, and food waste generated on campus is used to feed animals... At Yıldız Technical University Davutpaşa Campus, waste containers and special purpose containers are designed to help students, staff and guests to sort waste efficiently and simply. Thanks to the containers placed in the corridors of the faculties, wastes such as recyclable paper, metal and glass are separated without contamination with each other with the separation system at source. The waste oils generated in the cafeterias and cafeterias on campus that serve food are collected in sealed containers and delivered to authorized companies at regular intervals. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Medical and Dangerous Wastes 
 Similarly, hazardous wastes are handled in seven different types: solid-liquid laboratory wastes, fluorescent lamps, battery accumulators, cartridge-toners, used membrane filters, contaminated packaging and waste drugs. These hazardous wastes are collected in special boxes.  Expired electronic devices and batteries containing heavy metals are collected separately from household waste and collected In electronic waste and battery separation containers placed at the most frequently used points, especially at the entrances of the buildings,   . Materials containing hazardous materials such as laboratory wastes, used cartridges and fluorescent lamps are collected by the personnel responsible for the replacement of the relevant materials and stored in a special area. 
 Waste mask and glove boxes were placed at various points in order not to throw away the masks and gloves, which have been made mandatory due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which has affected the whole world, with household waste. These wastes are also collected together with medical wastes. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Organic Wastes Are Composted 
 What compost was,  was not known until a short time ago. However, this recycling method, which is the subject of even cartoons, is a very useful method, especially ensuring that food residues do not go to waste. At YTU, the twigs and twigs wastes generated during the landscaping of the open areas of the campus and the organic wastes generated during the preparation of meals in the cafeteria are composted in a compost machine located on the campus. This ensures that many wastes, from batteries to paper, from tomatoes to eggs, are correctly recycled on campus. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 Cooperation in Waste Management 
 The 5th Eurasian Waste Management Symposium, which provides a comprehensive overview of effective waste management strategies in Asian and European regions, was organized in cooperation with YTU and İSTAÇ. The symposium covers studies on all areas of waste management such as legislation, transport, treatment, recycling and reuse focuses for hazardous, medical and other types of waste. In partnership with YTU and De Montfort University,  led by faculty member Prof. Dr.Eyüp Debik and his team, the “UK-Turkey Capacity Building for Wastewater Treatment Integrated with Renewable Energy and Safer Reuse for Sustainable Communities” project was entitled to be supported by the Newton Fund. Environment and sustainability focused student clubs are actively operating within YTU. Waste food, plastic and paper are regularly collected within the framework of the “Star Transforms” project, which was initiated with the cooperation of Animal Rights, Social Responsibility, Economy and Environment Clubs. Waste food suitable for the health of the animals is collected and given to the dogs in Davutpaşa Campus. In addition, the collected plastic bottles and paper wastes are taken from YTU every day by the Esenler Municipality waste vehicle for recycling.

 Smart Campus and Digital Transformation 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Smart Campus and Digital Transformation 
 
 
 
 A+ 
 A- 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Environmentally Compatible Sustainable Living Areas 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A Smart And Green Campus 
 In addition to its quality education, Davutpaşa campus can be called a "Living Campus", with all its dynamics that not only support the individual development of students but also creates a spatial identity by separating itself from other places of its kind with its historical and natural assets, and the fact that it reflects all the vitality of the city as a science and culture center. In addition to all these, YTU also implements beautiful and functional applications in order to use the campus more effectively and efficiently. While aiming to create a unity with social living areas, a cultural center and educational areas in harmony with its environment and historical texture, it also includes the elements of being an environment-friendly, pedestrian-first barrier-free campus where green areas are protected, resource efficiency and sustainability principles are adopted, resulted in the development of a so-called ‘Living Campus.’ The creation of a sustainable campus was another target. A respectful approach to nature and people has been adopted in the environmental arrangements carried out with the understanding of a "Sustainable Campus" which is paying attention to ecological, social and economic dimensions; meticulous work has been carried out to protect the green areas in the campus and make them more qualified. Frameworks such as Turkey's Zero Waste Policy and the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were taken into consideration, and as a result, all YTU campuses, especially Davutpaşa Campus, were turned into sustainable living areas. 
 Digital Transformation 
 Yıldız Technical University has come a long way in digital transformation on its campuses with the aim of bringing the future to the present. New technologies applied on YTU campuses lead other universities and institutions. The prominent applications of YTU regarding digital transformation are as follows; 
 Super Wi-Fi Access 
 The entire Yıldız Technical University and Technopark campus area is covered with professional and industrial super wi-fi equipment. Students and Technopark company employees will meet with the new generation access form Super Wi-Fi infrastructure. 
 Mobile Wireless Access 
 Within the Yıldız Technical University Davutpaşa Campus and the Technopark Campus area, there is uninterrupted mobile wireless access even when you are on the move by bicycle. 
 Poll Editing with Wi-Fi Connection 
 At Davutpaşa Campus and Technopark Campus area, a survey form can be presented to anyone who will benefit from super wi-fi broadcasting. 
 Rest and Recharge Points 
 Smart benches which are placed in the resting areas provide ease of life on the campus. They run on solar energy which they can store for days and nights even when there is no sun, and they have a USB port as well. 
 Solar Lighting Pole 
 The lighting poles used in the campus are solar powered. In this way, electricity usage is minimized. 
 The Information System 
 With the information system used in the campus, you can view all the buildings on the land in their real locations, query all infrastructure and superstructure information and speed up the coordination between these units. Using the system, tracking the changed/ maintained/newly built and moved inventories is possible as well. As a result easier inventory and personnel management opportunities are provided by displaying them on a location-based map. 
 Online Library Reservation System 
 In the online library, students can make online reservations with their username and password, choose the lodge, table or room they want, make future reservations, and perform loan-return book transactions.

 Educational Experience on an Environmentally Friendly Campus 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Everything in college life begins and ends on campus. When you step through the door of our university, you will encounter a completely different world. While the “Living Campus” Davutpaşa offers students the opportunity to study in a historical and natural place; with its dormitory, green areas, and social structures, it is among the most beautiful campuses in the world. The campus, where green areas are protected, resource efficiency and sustainability principles are adopted, and which includes the elements of being a barrier-free campus with priority for pedestrians, maintains its existence in a structure that is friendly to the environment, people, and the future. Like other students, you will add value to our campus with your presence and uniqueness.

 Our Clubs Are Waiting for YTÜ Students 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yıldız Technical University, recognizing that attending classes alone does not make a university, has 73 clubs, all of which are run by students… Here, every student can find a club that matches their interests, ranging from mountaineering to physics, and from archery to the Development and Innovation Club. 
 
 
 
 
 Yıldız Technical University supports its universal approach to education through social, cultural, artistic, and athletic activities. The YTÜ Student Clubs, all of which are run entirely by students, help students develop in line with their interests, collaborate on projects, and enrich their social lives. There are 73 student clubs active across the university, spanning diverse fields from science to art, sports to engineering. To enhance the clubs’ physical facilities and bring them together in a shared space, the “Clubs Valley” project—designed by Prof. Dr. Deniz Erinsel Önder—has been implemented.

 Accommodation, Food, and Drink 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Accommodation, Food, and Drink 
 
 
 
 A+ 
 A- 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Possibility of Accommodation in High-Capacity and Quality Dormitories 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 When students from outside of İstanbul come to Yıldız Technical University, they find a comfortable, peaceful and safe environment. Çağdaş Yaşam Sennur Selçuk Öztap Female Dormitory for 72 students, İstanbul Kız Liseliler Female Dormitory for 42 students, and Şehide Türkan Türkmen Tekin Female Dormitory for 24 students at Davutpaşa Campus provide accommodation for a total of 138 students. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 138 
 Female students at 
Davutpaşa Campus 
 
 10  k

 YTU dining halls serve 
10 thousand students a day 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 High Standards of Food Service 
 Daily meals for students, administrative, and academic staff are prepared in kitchens on Yıldız and Davutpaşa campuses and served in dining halls. The food service is inspected by the nutrition unit personnel within the Department of Health Culture and Sports following the technical specifications, starting from the purchase phase of the goods and services until the end of the service. YTU cafeterias, which serve 10,000 people daily during the academic year, also serve dinner apart from lunch. 
 Yıldız Technical University Student Dormitories 
 Yıldız Technical University students are provided with shelter in comfortable, peaceful, and safe environments when they come from outside of the province. Davutpaşa Campus offers housing to a total of 131 students with Çağdaş Yaşam Sennur Selçuk Öztap Female Dormitory (for 72 bachelor's and master's degree students), İstanbul Kız Liseliler Male Dormitory ( for 42 doctoral and post-doctoral researchers) and Şehide Türkan Türkmen Tekin Female Dormitory (for 24 doctoral and post-doctoral researchers). 
 Davutpasa Çağdaş Yaşam Sennur Selçuk Öztap Dormitory 
 Located within the Davutpaşa Campus, the dormitory is a one-block female dormitory with 72 beds. Rooms are for 3 people; each room has a shower, WC, refrigerator, wardrobe, desk, and wireless internet system. The dormitory has a laundry room with washing machines, dryers, irons, ironing tables; a kitchen with a microwave, kettle, toaster, electric stove, water dispensers; a television room; and a study room. 
 Şehide Türkan Türkmen Tekin Female Dormitory 
 The dormitory at Davutpaşa Campus consists of one block and has a capacity of 24 beds. All apartments have 2 bedrooms, for 1 person or 2 people. The rooms are for 1 or 3 people... The dormitory has a ready-to-use kitchen, television (relaxation) room, bathroom, laundry, and dryer. 
 İstanbul Kız Liseliler Female Dormitory 
 The dormitory, which is located within Davutpaşa Campus, is a one-block female dormitory with 42 beds... The rooms are for 3 people, and each room has a shower, WC, refrigerator, wardrobe, desk, and wireless internet system. The dormitory also has a laundry room with washing machines and dryers, irons, ironing tables; a kitchen with a microwave, kettle, toaster, electric stove, water dispensers; a television room, and a study room.

 A+ 
 A- 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A Campus Designed for a Healthy Future and Barrier-Free Tomorrows: Davutpasa 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Sports Facilities Equipped with the Latest Technology are Open to Everyone 
 The period we are in has once again reminded the world how important health is. For a healthy body, regular exercise and a balanced diet are a must. The sports facilities that live up to the latest technology in the Davutpasa Campus of YTU are open to anyone who wants to do sports and keep fit. All students, academic and administrative staff, graduates and retirees can use the semi-olympic indoor swimming pool, fitness center, carpet pitch and tennis courts in Davutpasa Campus. In addition, the disabled can benefit from the sports facilities free of charge. 
 Modern Arrangement with Green Campus Concept 
 The projects implemented in the campus recreational studies were implemented in line with short and long-term structuring according to the principle of protecting the natural life on campus within the framework of the green campus concept. Life on campus has been organized in a comfortable and livable manner for disabled users of all ages, for the purpose of protecting and diversifying flora and fauna, locating animal shelters in suitable areas, container zones created to raise awareness of recycling, and an understanding of barrier-free life. Furthermore, in addition to indoor and outdoor sports areas, walking paths and bicycle tracks, natural living spaces that form integrity with landscape aesthetics, practices such as nature-friendly construction materials used for the recovery of waste water and rainwater, and green energy-supported lighting come to the forefront.

 Many Forms of Art, from Architecture to Music, Are Waiting for Yıldız Members 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 The Gateway to a Completely Different World: YTU Art Clubs 
 Culture and art life is also given great importance on YTU campuses. Academic life becomes more enjoyable and prosperous on campuses, where activities in many artistic fields, from architecture to music, are carried out. In addition, art clubs within YTU open the doors of a completely different world to students with various events they organize every year. 
 What are YTU Art Clubs Doing? 
 1002 Poetry and Fairy Tale Club (1002 ŞMK) 
 They organize conversations on poetry and literature and prepare book days and periodic fanzines. 
 Photography Club (FOK) 
 They take photos in historical areas and nature. In addition, they deliver photo printing workshops and organize trainings. 
 Traditional Arts Club (GESK) 
 They organize events by bringing together the students interested in traditional arts (Miniature, marbling etc.) and work to increase awareness on these arts. 
 Music Club 
 They organize choirs, concerts, and music competitions. In addition, the Pi community, affiliated with the Music Club, organizes museum and exhibition tours, talks on literature, supporting the socialization of its members. 
 Space and Art Kitchen Club (SPARK) 
 They organize projects that will highlight YTU's name in interdisciplinary fields. They are mainly technically oriented in their work. 
 Cinema Club 
 They organize film screenings and film festivals. 
 Turkish Music Club (MUSIKI) 
 They organize concerts and training in Turkish Folk and Art Music. 
 Yıldız Stage Club 
 Yıldız Stage aims to make university students love theater and make them see art as a part of their lives based on the nature of art.

 Under the slogan “Are you ready to be a star?”, YTÜ will host prospective students and their families at the Davutpaşa Campus during its 2026 Open House event.    From academic programs to international education opportunities, from technology teams to the entrepreneurship ecosystem, and from scholarships to campus life, YTÜ will share the opportunities it offers with prospective students between July 25 and 28, 2026.   -- Following today’s announcement of the 2026 Higher Education Institutions Exam (YKS) results by the Student Selection and Placement Center (ÖSYM), the countdown to the university application process has begun. Yıldız Technical University is organizing the 2026 Open House event for prospective students and their families preparing to make their university choices. The event, held under the motto “Are you ready to be a Star?”, will begin on Saturday, July 25, 2026, and will last four days.    As part of the YTÜ Open House, prospective students and their families will be hosted at the Historic Hamam Cultural Center and the Central Garden on the Davutpaşa Campus. Participants will have the opportunity to meet with YTÜ faculty, students, and alumni—including deans and department chairs—to receive firsthand information about departments, academic programs, campus life, and career opportunities after graduation.    Questions regarding the application process will be answered directly YTÜ’s faculties and departments will meet with prospective students at information booths set up at the Historic Hamam Cultural Center. Department faculty will provide comprehensive information on academic staff, course content, language of instruction, preparatory programs, laboratory infrastructure, applied education processes, and research opportunities.   Prospective students will be able to ask faculty members about any topics they are curious about during the application process—ranging from double major and minor programs to Erasmus+ mobility, from internship opportunities to industry partnerships, and from student projects to career paths after graduation.   Current YTÜ students will also share their experiences with applicants regarding course programs, club activities, technology teams, campus life, international exchange programs, and what it’s like to be a YTÜ student. This will allow young people to evaluate the departments they are considering not only based on academic information but also through the lens of student experiences. An Invitation to Prospective Students from Rector Debik YTÜ Rector Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, noting that choosing a university is a crucial decision that shapes young people’s educational and career journeys, invited prospective students and their families to the open house events. Prof. Dr. Debik stated:   “Choosing a university is the most important step our young people take toward the future. We believe it is valuable for our young people to make their choice by thoroughly evaluating all aspects of universities—including their educational programs, academic staff, research opportunities, clubs and technology teams, international opportunities (particularly Erasmus+), and campus life. As Yıldız Technical University, we possess a strong ecosystem that transforms knowledge into technology, ideas into projects, and talents into social value. We hope that our prospective students will meet with our faculty and students, find direct answers to their questions, and experience what it means to be a part of Yıldız on our campus. We look forward to welcoming all young people who wish to learn, create, and shape the future—along with their families—to our historic Davutpaşa Campus.”   115 Years of Academic Heritage Yıldız Technical University carries its 115 years of academic heritage into the future through contemporary education, scientific research, and technology development initiatives. With its 10 faculties, 3 institutes, School of Foreign Languages, nearly 1,800 faculty members, nearly 40,000 students, and over 300 laboratories, YTÜ offers a multifaceted education and research environment.   By integrating undergraduate education with research, practical application, and project development, the university enables students to apply their academic knowledge to solving real-world problems. Prospective students will have the opportunity to gain a close-up look at the university’s educational philosophy and research infrastructure during YTÜ Open House Days.   YTÜ’s Global Rise Will Be Highlighted for Prospective Students Continuing its upward trend in international academic rankings, YTÜ is strengthening its global visibility in the fields of education and research year after year. Having climbed 102 spots in the QS 2027 World University Rankings, YTÜ is ranked 634th globally and 9th in Turkey. In the THE 2026 World University Rankings, the university was placed in the 601–800 range and ranked 4th among state universities in Turkey.   Ranked 3rd among technical universities in the YÖK Research Universities Ranking, YTÜ is strengthening its scientific research through national and international projects, university-industry collaborations, and high-quality publications. Detailed information on the ranking results, research opportunities, and international academic collaborations will be shared with prospective students and their families during the Open House Days.   YTÜ: Turkey’s Leader in Erasmus+ Positioning internationalization as a key element of its education and research strategy, Yıldız Technical University continues to lead in Erasmus+ student mobility. For the past three years, YTÜ has stood out as the university sending the most students from Turkey under the Erasmus+ program. The university boasts a strong international structure, encompassing over 300 partner universities worldwide, more than 700 international cooperation agreements, and an academic collaboration network reaching over 100 countries. YTÜ researchers also contribute to Europe’s scientific collaboration networks through their membership in over 100 COST actions.   Under the Erasmus+ program, 1,820 YTÜ students were sent abroad for study and internship mobility during the previous academic year. During the same period, 460 international students studied at YTÜ. Through its Erasmus+ initiatives, the university secured 12.3 million euros in grant funding. Prospective students will be able to learn about Erasmus+ programs, study and internship mobility abroad, international agreements, and application processes during the open house events.   Technology Teams to Gather in the Central Courtyard YTÜ’s Davutpaşa Central Courtyard will host the university’s technology teams and student clubs throughout the open house days. Unmanned aerial vehicles, autonomous race cars, robotic systems, and various engineering projects developed by YTÜ teams—which have achieved success at TEKNOFEST and international technology competitions—will be showcased to prospective students. Participants will be able to speak with the students who developed the vehicles and systems to learn about project development processes, teamwork, and competition experiences.   YTÜ students submitted 444 project applications to TEKNOFEST 2025. While 52 “Yıldızlı” teams advanced to the finals in the competitions, “Yıldızlı” students increased the number of awards they won from 11 the previous year to 27. These results serve as indicators of the university’s strong culture, where students can participate in technology development and high-quality project creation processes even during their undergraduate years.   YTÜ’s 73 student clubs will also meet with prospective students during the open house days through activities ranging from science and technology to culture and art, sports, social responsibility, and entrepreneurship.   Student Ideas Turn into Projects and Startups During the open house, Yıldız Technical University’s entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystem will also be introduced to prospective students. YTÜ Yıldız Technopark, the YTÜ Technology Transfer Office, YTU Startup House, ETP—a new addition to the YTÜ ecosystem—and the “Yıldız Explorers” entrepreneurship program, which is open to all universities, support students in turning their ideas into projects, products, and technology startups.    Students can participate in entrepreneurship training during their university years, develop their business ideas, create prototypes, and receive mentorship from experienced experts in their fields.   Nearly 750 technology companies, academic startups, and entrepreneurship programs operating within the YTU Yıldız Technopark TGB area create a comprehensive production environment where students can bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and industry needs.   During the open house, prospective students will have the opportunity to closely examine the stages through which an idea at the university can evolve into a project, a product, and a startup.   Students Gain Exposure to the Professional World Before Graduation YTÜ’s KOOP Education Model enables students to establish direct contact with the industry while still pursuing their undergraduate studies. Students gain real-world work experience at institutions and organizations partnered with the university, providing them with the opportunity to apply their academic knowledge in a professional setting.   Thanks to the KOOP Education Model, YTÜ students develop their professional competencies, gain a close understanding of industry expectations, and prepare for their career journeys during their university years. The scope of the model, application processes, and the opportunities it offers to students will be shared in detail with prospective students during the information sessions.   A strong alumni network supports your career journey Yıldız graduates continue their work in a wide range of fields—from engineering to architecture, education to economics, and basic sciences to technology entrepreneurship—both in Turkey and around the world.   The university’s strong ties with the industry and its extensive alumni network provide Yıldız students with a vital professional environment where they can access internships, projects, mentorship, and career opportunities. Prospective students will also be able to learn about the fields of work and career paths of graduates from various departments.   Scholarship Support for Students from the YTÜ Foundation The YTÜ Foundation, one of the long-standing institutions of the YTÜ Family, supports students’ educational journeys through scholarship programs. The Outstanding Achievement Scholarship, intended for students who achieved high scores on the YKS and chose YTÜ, as well as the Equal Opportunity Scholarship—which prioritizes educational needs—and the meal scholarship are all available to YTÜ students. During the open house events, prospective students and their families will be provided with information regarding the scope of the scholarships, application requirements, and evaluation processes.   History, nature, and student life all on one campus YTÜ climbed 11 spots in the UI GreenMetric 2025 World University Rankings, becoming the 48th most sustainable university in the world and the 2nd in Turkey. The Yıldız and Davutpaşa campuses, distinguished by their historic buildings, green spaces, and modern educational infrastructure, offer students a rich university life that encompasses not only academic development but also social, cultural, and athletic opportunities.   Student clubs, technology teams, sports facilities, the library, social spaces, and events held throughout the year create a dynamic campus atmosphere where Yıldız students can thrive in various fields.   While the Beşiktaş Yıldız Campus, located in the heart of Istanbul, is easily accessible from all directions, the Davutpaşa Campus can be reached directly by metro and bus. On campus, a shuttle service operates with 8 buses running every 10 minutes throughout the academic year.    Yıldız Prospective Students Are Invited to the Davutpaşa Campus We invite prospective Yıldız students and their families to the Davutpaşa Campus to make an informed decision about their university choice, hear about the departments directly from faculty members, benefit from the experiences of current Yıldız students, and get an up-close look at YTÜ’s ecosystem of education, research, internationalization, technology, and entrepreneurship.    YTÜ 2026 Open House 📅   Date:  July 25–28, 2026 🕙   Time:  10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. 📍   Location:  YTÜ Davutpaşa Campus, Historical Hamam Cultural Center, and Central Garden   Detailed information about the YTÜ Open House and the opportunities offered by the university is available at  tanitim.yildiz.edu.tr  and  www.yildiz.edu.tr .

 We graduated more than 5,000 undergraduate and graduate students during the ceremonies we held at the YTÜ Davutpaşa Campus from July 6 to 10, 2026. More than 22,000 family members and friends of our students shared in the excitement of the ceremonies, during which our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, presented plaques to the top three students in each department. As Yıldız Technical University, we held our graduation ceremonies for the 2025–2026 academic year from July 6–10, 2026, at the Davutpaşa Congress and Culture Center. As we sent off 5,205 students graduating from our 10 faculties and 3 institutes into the future, we hosted 22,870 family members and guests of our students on our campus over the course of five days. The graduation ceremonies were attended by our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik; our Vice Rector for Education and Teaching, Prof. Dr. Vatan Karakaya; our Vice Rector for Administration, Prof. Dr. Ahmet Göksel Ağargün; our Vice Rector for Research and Planning, Prof. Dr. Güleda Engin; our Chief Advisor to the Rector, Prof. Dr. Özer Çınar; our Dean of Students, Prof. Dr. Gamze Varank; as well as institute directors, deans, department chairs, and our faculty members. Plaques Presented by Our Rector to Top-Ranking Graduates During the graduation ceremonies, where our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, addressed the students and their families, plaques were presented to the top three students in each department. While the top-ranking students received their plaques from our Rector, Prof. Dr. Debik, our undergraduate graduates were presented with their diplomas by deans and department chairs, and our master’s and doctoral graduates received their diplomas from our institute directors.   “Turn the Knowledge You Have Gained into Social Benefit” In his speeches at the graduation ceremonies, our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, thanked our faculty members for their guidance and the families for their sacrifices.  Calling on our graduates to keep their scientific curiosity alive, to continuously develop themselves, and to transform knowledge into social benefit, Rector Eyüp Debik said, “Never give up on researching, questioning, and learning. In the age of artificial intelligence, your greatest strength will be your ability to think critically, generate original ideas, strengthen your intellectual foundation, and apply your knowledge for the benefit of humanity,” he said. Advising our distinguished graduates to maintain strong ties with YTÜ and the YTÜ Foundation, Rector Debik said, “Be sure to join the Alumni Platform run by our YTÜ Alumni Coordination Office, make a point of attending the annual alumni reunions, and strive throughout your lives to be a strong part of the Yıldız Family and to create value. Let knowledge be your guide and your conscience your compass. I congratulate each and every one of you from the bottom of my heart,” he said. We Welcomed Our Graduates’ Families and Friends During the five-day graduation ceremonies, family members and friends shared in our students’ joy. At the ceremonies, which saw 22,870 attendees, our graduates received their diplomas, tossed their caps into the air together, and celebrated this special day—symbolizing their university years—with their loved ones. We Sent Our Stars Off into the Future We sent off our graduates—who were educated in various disciplines ranging from engineering to architecture and from the natural sciences to the social sciences—into their new lives, equipped with the academic knowledge, research culture, and professional competence they acquired at our university. As Yıldız Technical University, we took great joy in graduating our students as individuals who develop ideas, conduct research, devise solutions, and embrace the responsibility of adding value to society. We Wish Our Stars Success in Life With the graduation ceremonies of the 2025–2026 academic year, we have expanded our YTÜ family with 5,205 new graduates. We believe that our graduates will maintain their connection with our university throughout their lives and will undertake projects that add value to our country and humanity through their knowledge and experience; we wish each and every one of our “Stars” a future filled with health, success, and well-being.  A delegation from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, one of the world’s leading universities, visited Yıldız Technical University. The discussions focused on new collaborations in artificial intelligence, medical robotics, smart manufacturing, student exchange, and international R&D projects. A delegation from Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), one of the world’s most prestigious institutions of higher education, visited Yıldız Technical University (YTÜ) to engage in comprehensive discussions aimed at strengthening the strategic partnership between the two universities. This visit, which served as a continuation of the strategic partnership established during our Rector’s inaugural visit to China, explored opportunities for collaboration in numerous fields, ranging from artificial intelligence and medical robotics to smart manufacturing technologies and international student mobility. A new roadmap was established following the agreement The program began with a tour of YTÜ’s Davutpaşa Campus. Subsequently, our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, hosted Shanghai Jiao Tong University Vice Rector Prof. Dr. Zhaoguo Zhang and his accompanying delegation. Also participating in the program were Prof. Dr. Qian WANG, Deputy Director of the Office of Global Cooperation and Exchange; Prof. Dr. Weidong CHEN, Associate Dean of the Institute of Medical Robotics; Dr. Hailei CHEN, Asia Affairs Specialist at the Office of Global Cooperation and Exchange; and Ms. Guifang QI, Head of the International Relations Office at the SJTU Paris Elite Institute of Technology.  During the meeting, the work carried out following the previously signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was reviewed, and the strategic roadmap for future cooperation between the two universities was discussed.  Artificial intelligence and medical robotics among priority areas Following the meeting at the Rector’s Office, a roundtable session was held, bringing together academics and administrators. During the meeting, opportunities for joint work in the areas of artificial intelligence, medical robotics, control systems, smart manufacturing technologies, international student mobility, and Turkey-China academic collaborations were evaluated in detail. In addition to YTÜ Rector Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, the meeting was attended by Vice Rector Prof. Dr. Vatan Karakaya, Chief Advisor to the Rector Prof. Dr. Özer Çınar, Dean of the Faculty of Electrical and Electronic Engineering Prof. Dr. Ahmet Faruk Bakan, YTÜ Yıldız Technopark Deputy General Manager Prof. Dr. Cengiz Kaya, and relevant faculty members. YTÜ’s innovation ecosystem was showcased on-site Following the meetings, the delegation from Shanghai Jiao Tong University received information about YTÜ Yıldız Technopark, the Technology Transfer Office (TTO), and the Industrial Design and Prototyping Center (ETP). As part of the program, the delegation was introduced to YTÜ Yıldız Technopark’s entrepreneurship ecosystem, collaborations with Turkish industry, and projects carried out in various technology fields. The delegation then visited the Industrial Design and Prototyping Center (ETP) and the Central Laboratory to examine the research infrastructure firsthand. Advanced technology laboratories were inspected As part of the visit, the SJTU delegation also toured the advanced technology research laboratories operating at YTÜ. During the tour, information was shared about the research infrastructure focused on advanced materials technologies, particularly the Nanotechnology Laboratory, the Glass Technologies Laboratory, and the Coating Technologies Laboratory. New steps toward joint projects and student exchange At the conclusion of the meetings, the two universities reached an agreement on joint work in areas that will take their collaboration to the next level. Accordingly, it was decided to develop student and faculty exchange programs, evaluate new scholarship opportunities under the China Scholarship Council (CSC) and SJTU scholarship programs, and identify areas for joint research, developing project-based education and short-term exchange programs with SPEIT and Global College, and preparing joint international projects under TÜBİTAK, Erasmus+, and Horizon Europe. The visit is expected to make a significant contribution to strengthening long-term strategic partnerships between Yıldız Technical University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University in the fields of education, research, technology development, and internationalization.  About Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) is a higher education institution founded in 1896 and recognized as one of China’s most established and prestigious research universities. Affiliated with the Chinese Ministry of Education, the university ranks among the world’s leading research centers in numerous fields, including engineering, artificial intelligence, medicine, robotics, materials science, computer science, and business. The university holds a strong global position thanks to its scientific publication performance, international research collaborations, and technology-driven innovation efforts. Shanghai Jiao Tong University ranks 40th in the World University Rankings.

 Associate Professor Dr. Ali Can Zaman, a faculty member in the Department of Metallurgy and Materials Engineering at YTÜ, and his research team have developed an electroactive hybrid polymer that could contribute to new-generation battery technologies offering long life and fast charging capabilities. The invention, registered by the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office, is intended for use not only in energy storage but also in fields such as carbon capture and water purification. Our university has achieved yet another significant milestone in the field of energy storage technologies. The electroactive hybrid polymer developed by our Department of Metallurgy and Materials Engineering faculty member Assoc. Prof. Dr. Ali Can Zaman and his research team stands out as a significant innovation that could contribute to the development of next-generation battery technologies with longer lifespans and faster charging capabilities. The work, registered by the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office, holds potential for use not only in energy storage technologies but also in various other fields such as carbon capture and water purification. A novel polymerization method for next-generation batteries has been developed As part of their research, our university’s team developed a new-generation hybrid polymer by reacting elemental sulfur with acetone using a unique polymerization method. The developed material retains sulfur’s energy storage capacity while also incorporating the advantages provided by organic compounds. Thus, a new class of materials has been introduced that could contribute to long-lasting, fast-charging, and high-performance battery technologies. "We have obtained a new polymer with hybrid properties" Commenting on the study to the Anadolu Agency (AA), Assoc. Prof. Dr. Ali Can Zaman, a faculty member in the Department of Metallurgy and Materials Engineering, stated that the primary goal of the research was to improve the performance of energy storage systems. Noting that they have focused their research specifically on lithium-sulfur batteries, Zaman made the following assessment: "Using this method, we produced polymeric materials by inducing a reaction between elemental sulfur and organic compounds that would not normally react under standard conditions. The new material we developed retains sulfur’s energy storage properties while also incorporating the distinct properties derived from the organic compounds. In fact, we have developed a new polymer that exhibits hybrid properties." Assoc. Prof. Dr. Zaman emphasized that, following sufficient optimization, the developed electroactive polymer could make significant contributions to the development of batteries with longer lifespans and faster charging and discharging capabilities. The study offers a unique approach to the scientific literature Noting that the method developed as part of the research offers a scientifically original approach, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Zaman noted that although similar studies have been conducted in the past, using this method to react a simple organic molecule such as acetone with elemental sulfur has paved the way for the emergence of a new class of materials in the literature. It offers applications beyond energy storage The hybrid polymer developed at our university is not limited to battery technologies. The research team’s studies have demonstrated that the material yields successful results in carbon dioxide capture applications, while its sulfur-containing structure also indicates significant potential in water purification technologies. It is believed that the material, which can exhibit sponge-like behavior—particularly in the removal of heavy metals such as mercury from water—could be effectively utilized in environmental technologies in the future. In addition, research is ongoing into the use of the developed polymer in gas separation and adsorption applications. The goal is to make a multifaceted contribution to energy and environmental technologies The electroactive hybrid polymer, developed at our university and registered by the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office, is attracting attention as a versatile material that can be used in many strategic areas such as energy storage, carbon capture, gas separation, and water treatment. The study is expected to make significant contributions to the development of sustainable energy technologies and environmentally friendly solutions. We wholeheartedly congratulate our faculty member, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Ali Can Zaman, and his research team for bringing this original work—which contributes to next-generation energy storage technologies—to fruition; we wish them continued success in their efforts to shape our country’s future in the fields of science, technology, and sustainability.

 Yıldız Technical University organized the “July 15 Epic” program—featuring a panel discussion, an exhibition, and heroic folk songs—as part of the July 15 Democracy and National Unity Day celebrations. Prof. Dr. Erhan Afyoncu, Rector of the National Defense University, who participated in the program, stated, “This uprising was part of FETÖ’s plan to occupy and fragment Turkey.” On the 10th anniversary of the treacherous coup attempt targeting the national will, we commemorated our martyrs and expressed our gratitude to our veterans through the “July 15 Epic” program held at the YTÜ Davutpaşa Historic Hamam Cultural Center. Prior to the program, the July 15 Democracy and National Unity Exhibition was inaugurated. The July 15 Democracy and National Unity Day program, which began with a recitation from the Holy Quran, featured Prof. Dr. Erhan Afyoncu, Rector of the National Defense University, as a guest speaker. The program continued with a “Songs of Heroism” concert performed by YTÜ Lecturer Dr. Erdal Şahin.   Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik: July 15 is the moment when the spirit of the National Struggle was reaffirmed Delivering the opening remarks, our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, stated that July 15 marks a historic turning point when the consciousness of being a nation regained its strength. Noting that July 15 left indelible marks on our collective memory, Debik said: “July 15 is the night when the national will shaped history. It is an exceptional moment when consciousness transformed into courage. July 15 is the date when the sense of national identity was reclaimed. It is the night when collective memory converged with collective courage. It is a turning point where differences united under a single national will. In short, July 15 is the moment when the spirit of the National Struggle was re-manifested in the 21st century.” “Our nation stood up for its democracy and independence” Debik stated that on the night of July 15, the Turkish nation, under the leadership of our President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and alongside the security forces and our heroic army, defended its democracy, independence, and constitutional order, adding that the will demonstrated in the squares has gone down in history. Debik said, “I commemorate our martyrs, who demonstrated that will at the cost of their lives, with mercy and gratitude, and I wish our veterans good health and a long life.” “The Will Is Ours, the Victory Is Ours” Emphasis Noting that this year’s commemoration programs were held under the theme “The Will Is Ours, the Victory Is Ours,” Prof. Dr. Debik said that this theme most powerfully expresses the Turkish nation’s understanding of independence throughout history. Prof. Dr. Debik said, “The will is ours because the Turkish nation has never wavered in its resolve to defend its homeland and independence throughout history. Victory is ours because this nation has won all its victories through its courage, self-sacrifice, and unshakable faith.” “We are uniting science with a sense of national responsibility” Emphasizing that YTÜ is a university that produces science and technology while also nurturing individuals committed to national values, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik said, “We embrace a higher education philosophy that unites knowledge with justice, academia with conscience, and science with a sense of national responsibility. While educating young people who develop technology, conduct research, and achieve international success, we also view raising individuals who are loyal to their homeland, flag, nation, and national will as one of our primary responsibilities.” Prof. Dr. Erhan Afyoncu: July 15 Was Part of a Plan to Invade Turkey Prof. Dr. Erhan Afyoncu, Rector of the National Defense University, made notable remarks during the discussion titled “July 15: History, Memory, and National Will,” moderated by YTÜ Lecturer Dr. Erdal Şahin. Emphasizing that July 15 was not a classic military coup attempt, Rector Afyoncu stated, “I do not believe we have yet fully grasped the significance of July 15 in Turkey. This uprising was not a coup or a coup attempt in the classical sense. It was part of FETÖ’s long-term plan aimed at occupying Turkey, fragmenting the country, and plunging it into chaos,” he said. “The goal was to plunge Turkey into civil war” In his speech, Afyoncu offered his assessment of the night of the coup and noted that the plan was not limited to simply seizing power. Stating that the goals included opening the borders, directing terrorist organizations into Turkey, and creating a prolonged environment of chaos, Afyoncu described the events as a comprehensive operation with international dimensions. “FETÖ infiltrated the state over the course of decades” Afyoncu noted that the organization had systematically placed students in military high schools and military academies, particularly starting in the 1970s, and said it had pursued a long-term strategy of staffing key positions. Afyoncu stated that organization members were systematically assigned to various fields—from law enforcement to the judiciary, and from education to the Turkish Armed Forces—and noted that despite investigations conducted in 1982 and 1986, the network could not be dismantled. Prof. Dr. Erhan Afyoncu noted that the organization increased its influence within the state during the Ergenekon and Balyoz trials, adding that a large number of military personnel were purged during this period. He noted that the unusual departure of hundreds of students from the Military Academy in certain years was also one of the indicators of this systematic purge. “Our people’s resistance thwarted the grand plan” Afyoncu said that the people’s swift mobilization into the streets on the night of July 15 was decisive in the failure of the coup attempt, noting that the people heroically thwarted the attempt by lying in front of tanks and acting in concert with security forces. Prof. Dr. Afyoncu said, “July 15 represents a significant act of resistance in the history of world democracy. That night once again demonstrated that no power other than the elected will can seize control of the government by force of arms.” “The FETÖ threat has not completely ended” Concluding his speech, Prof. Dr. Afyoncu noted that it is not possible to say the organization has been completely eradicated, adding that traces of its structure persist in various fields, particularly within universities. Stressing the need for the public to remain vigilant, Prof. Dr. Afyoncu concluded his remarks by emphasizing that loyalty to the state, the nation, and the flag is crucial for Turkey’s future. July 15 Exhibition The program, which featured a concert titled “Songs of Heroism” by YTÜ Lecturer Dr. Erdal Şahin, also included the opening of the “July 15 Democracy and National Unity Exhibition.” The exhibition, held at the Historic Hamam Cultural Center, will be open to visitors throughout the week.

 The "BBGNight-TR" project, coordinated by Yıldız Technical University, has been awarded funding under the European Union’s Horizon Europe Program. The 24-month project, to be carried out in partnership with Istanbul Technical University, Gazi University, and the Ministry of National Education, aims to bring science and society together in the fields of climate change, health, and digital transformation. Yıldız Technical University (YTÜ) has achieved yet another significant milestone under Horizon Europe, one of the European Union’s most prestigious programs in the fields of research and innovation. The BBGNight-TR (Science & Future Night: Engaging Researchers and Citizens in Climate, Health, and Digital Transitions in Türkiye) project, prepared under the coordination of Prof. Dr. Afşin Yusuf Çetinkaya, has been awarded funding under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) – European Researchers’ Night and Researchers at Schools (MSCA & Citizens) call for proposals. The project, to be carried out under the coordination of Yıldız Technical University, will include Istanbul Technical University, Gazi University, and the Ministry of National Education as project partners. Numerous scientific and social events will be held Over the course of the 24-month project, European Researchers’ Night events, Researchers at Schools activities, citizen science initiatives, science communication events, science cafés, interactive exhibitions, and interdisciplinary science demonstrations will be held. The project aims to establish a sustainable science communication ecosystem that strengthens the transfer of knowledge between researchers, educational institutions, decision-makers, and the public, and to promote the principles of open science and responsible research and innovation at the grassroots level.  A bridge for social engagement will be built Through BBGNight-TR, a strong bridge will be built between scientific knowledge production and social engagement on the themes of climate change, health, and digital transformation; to increase researchers’ direct engagement with society, develop science literacy, encourage young people’s participation in the research and innovation ecosystem, and strengthen Turkey’s international research and innovation capacity in line with the priorities of the European Research Area.  Aligned with the European Union’s priorities BBGNight-TR was designed to be consistent with the European Union’s European Green Deal, Digital Europe vision, and EU Missions. Through the science communication and citizen engagement models to be developed under the project, the goal is to promote the principles of open science and responsible research and innovation across society and to increase the societal impact of science. In this regard, BBGNight-TR stands out not only as a project that supports scientific research but also as a significant European Union initiative that strengthens sustainable collaboration among universities, public institutions, and society, and contributes to Turkey’s international research and innovation ecosystem.

 NEWS 
 Strategic cooperation between YTÜ and the Silesian University of Technology in Poland is growing stronger 
 
 
 
 13 July 2026 Monday 15:34

 Prof. Dr. Marek Pawełczyk, Rector of the Silesian University of Technology—one of Poland’s leading institutions of higher education—visited our university. The visit, which marked a new phase of the strategic partnership initiated at the 1st Turkey-Poland Rectors’ Forum, the visit marked a new phase in the strategic partnership. Discussions focused on European Union joint projects, student and faculty exchanges, joint degree programs, and academic collaborations planned to be implemented initially among six faculties. Prof. Dr. Marek Pawełczyk, Rector of Silesian University of Technology—one of Poland’s long-established institutions of higher education—visited our university along with his academic delegation. The delegation included Prof. Dr. Sebastian Werle, Vice Rector for Research and International Cooperation; Prof. Dr. Tomasz Bradecki, Dean of the Faculty of Architecture; Dean of the Faculty of Civil Engineering Prof. Dr. Barbara Klemczak, Dean of the Faculty of Transportation and Aviation Engineering Prof. Dr. Grzegorz Sierpinski, and Dean of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering Prof. Dr. Marcin Adamiak. Continuation of the process that began in Ankara Rector Pawełczyk and his delegation were welcomed by our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik; our Vice Rectors, Prof. Dr. Vatan Karakaya, Prof. Dr. Güleda Engin, our Research Projects Coordinator Prof. Dr. Cengiz Kaya, and our International Relations Coordinator Dr. Murat Turhan. This visit, which serves as a continuation of the strategic partnership initiated at the 1st Turkey-Poland Rectors’ Forum, organized by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), and further developed through our Rector’s visit to Poland, served as a continuation of this strategic partnership. During the visit, comprehensive discussions were held aimed at further strengthening the collaboration between the two universities through concrete projects.  As part of the visit, discussions were held to develop the strategic partnership between the two universities. Evaluations were conducted regarding European Union joint projects, student and faculty mobility, the implementation of joint degree programs, and the launch of joint academic and scientific studies initially involving six faculties. Joint efforts will be made in project applications During the meetings, a roadmap to ensure that the strategic partnership between the two universities yields concrete results was discussed in detail. While jointly evaluating upcoming international project calls, common strategies were established for accessing international funding sources, particularly from the European Union. At the same time, plans were made to conduct project application processes simultaneously and to coordinate joint project teams.  Laboratories and innovation infrastructure under review The progress made to date by the joint research groups established within the two universities was comprehensively analyzed. While processes were reviewed to ensure more efficient execution of ongoing work, assessments were also conducted regarding new research areas and collaborative working models.  The visiting delegation toured the YTÜ Central Laboratory, the Industrial Design and Prototyping Center (ETP), and YTÜ Yıldız Technopark to assess the infrastructure capabilities. The goal is to enable the shared use of the two universities’ research infrastructure in a complementary manner. A strategic alliance to create global impact As two strong institutions with Research University status, the goal is not only to develop academic relations between Turkey and Poland but also to build a high-quality R&D ecosystem that will make an impact on the global academic stage. In this context, high-impact scientific publications, value-added patents, international research projects, and interdisciplinary innovation initiatives are among the top priorities. The ongoing discussions with Silesian University of Technology are viewed as one of the most important steps toward a genuine strategic partnership that will enhance both universities’ research capacity, strengthen their international visibility, and produce tangible scientific outcomes. Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik: We Are Strengthening Internationalization Through Strategic Partnerships Our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, expressed his satisfaction with the visit and stated that the strong communication established between the two universities will lay the groundwork for multifaceted and sustainable academic collaborations in the future. In his remarks, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik said: “I would like to thank Prof. Dr. Marek Pawełczyk, Rector of Silesian University of Technology, for his kind visit and his valuable remarks about our university. As Yıldız Technical University, we aim to strengthen our internationalization efforts not only through student and faculty mobility but also through joint research, knowledge sharing, and strategic academic collaborations. I sincerely believe that the strong communication we have established between our two universities will lead to sustainable joint projects and long-term collaborations.” “We aim to strengthen academic collaborations through concrete projects” Prof. Dr. Marek Pawełczyk, Rector of Silesian University of Technology, attended the graduation ceremony of our Faculty of Shipbuilding and Maritime Sciences as part of his visit and addressed our students. In his speech, Prof. Dr. Pawełczyk stated that the strong rapport he had established with our Rector, Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik, laid the foundation for a strategic partnership between the two universities, and noted that they view Yıldız Technical University as a reliable and strong academic partner. Prof. Dr. Pawełczyk explained that they had come to Turkey with a large delegation to get to know our university better, strengthen academic collaborations through concrete projects, and expand areas of joint research. emphasized their belief that joint efforts in the fields of education, research, and internationalization would yield significant benefits for both universities. In his remarks, Prof. Dr. Pawełczyk said: “After Rector Prof. Dr. Eyüp Debik visited our university with his delegation and we met on various occasions, he sincerely invited me to visit your university. A strong friendship has developed between us, and our collaboration is growing stronger every day. The purpose of this visit is to get to know your university closely, establish new academic contacts, evaluate the details of our collaboration, and establish a long-term, strong partnership. Since there are so many universities in the world, we select our strategic partners with great care. I wholeheartedly believe that Yıldız Technical University is among our strategic partners and that together we have laid the solid foundations for long-term collaborations.” The Strategic Alliance Between Yıldız Technical University and Silesian University of Technology The 1st Turkey-Poland Rectors’ Forum, organized by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), served as the platform where the first seeds of the strategic partnership between YTÜ and Silesian University of Technology were sown.    Following the initial contact at the forum, a delegation from Yıldız Technical University paid a working visit to Silesian University of Technology with the aim of combining academic and scientific potential. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed during this visit went beyond being a mere goodwill document to form the basis of a direct action plan. In the initial phase of the collaboration between the two universities, the goal was to bring together researchers with strong academic expertise in engineering and advanced technology into joint working groups. To this end, online meetings were held to analyze the research capacities of both universities and form teams to conduct joint scientific research.  Furthermore, in line with the academic expertise of both universities, an agreement was reached to establish multidisciplinary project teams that will prepare joint applications for national and international funding sources, primarily Horizon Europe, TÜBİTAK, and bilateral international cooperation programs. The goal is to develop sustainable R&D projects between the two research universities and to make more effective use of international funding sources.
